title: Qualified Intermediary Coordination
name: Qualified Intermediary Coordination
metaTitle: Qualified Intermediary Coordination in Oklahoma City, OK
metaDescription: We coordinate directly with your qualified intermediary on Oklahoma City 1031 transactions so escrow, timing, and identification stay lined up correctly.

sections.html: You don't touch the sale proceeds at any point in a 1031 exchange. The qualified intermediary holds them, and getting that relationship set up correctly before your relinquished property closes is the single most important coordination step in the whole process. We work alongside your chosen intermediary on the Oklahoma City side of the transaction, keeping the exchange agreement, the escrow instructions, and your closing schedule lined up so nothing forces you into constructive receipt of funds. It's the kind of coordination that looks simple on paper and unravels fast if any one piece slips.

sections.heading: Why the Intermediary Has to Be in Place Before Closing
sections.html:
The exchange agreement needs to be signed before your relinquished property closes, not after, and the intermediary can't be someone disqualified under the rules, such as your own agent, employee, or close family member. Sale proceeds go straight into the intermediary's escrow account rather than to you, and that sequence has to hold up exactly, since there's no fixing it after the fact if funds land in the wrong place even briefly.

We confirm the intermediary's independence and the escrow setup ourselves before your closing date is finalized, so this isn't a detail left for the title company to catch at the last minute.

sections.heading: What We Coordinate Directly With Your Intermediary
sections.html:
Once your intermediary is selected, we track the pieces that have to move in the right order on an Oklahoma City closing:

  • Timing of the exchange agreement signature against your closing date
  • Wire instructions and escrow account confirmation before funds move
  • Identification notice delivery and confirmation of receipt within the 45-day window
  • Replacement property purchase agreement assignment language
  • Closing statement review so proceeds route through the intermediary correctly
  • Partial-interest or multi-property allocation instructions across your identification list

Each item gets confirmed in writing, so there's a paper trail if a question comes up later about how the exchange was structured.

sections.heading: Where Facilities-Level Thinking Helps This Process
sections.html: Coordinating a qualified intermediary, a title company, and a lender on the same calendar isn't that different from running multiple vendors on one job. We track it the same way you'd track punch list items across trades, following up on outstanding pieces before they become a closing delay rather than after the schedule has already slipped. That habit of chasing loose ends early is what keeps a multi-party closing from turning into a last-minute scramble.

sections.heading: Constructive Receipt: The Mistake That Ends an Exchange
sections.html:
Constructive receipt is the mistake that turns a clean exchange into a taxable sale, and it happens when proceeds touch your own account or you gain control over them, even briefly. Seller concessions, earnest money, and security deposit prorations all need to route through the intermediary correctly, and we flag any closing statement language that would put funds in your hands instead of theirs before the closing table, not after.

This is an easy trap for otherwise well-organized investors, since a title company can default to its standard closing statement template without adjusting it for an exchange, so we review that document specifically rather than assuming it was built with your intermediary's escrow in mind.

sections.heading: Aligning the 45-Day and 180-Day Clock With Your Intermediary's Paperwork
sections.html: Both the 45-day identification window and the 180-day exchange period run from the date your relinquished property closes, and extensions are rare outside specific disaster relief situations. We make sure the intermediary's paperwork reflects the exact closing date so your deadlines are calculated correctly from day one, not adjusted later when a discrepancy surfaces during your identification or closing window.

faqs.q: Can I use a friend or my own accountant as the qualified intermediary?
faqs.a: Generally no, since anyone who has acted as your agent, employee, or certain related parties within the prior two years is disqualified from serving as your intermediary. We help you confirm your chosen intermediary meets the independence requirement before the exchange agreement is signed, since disqualification discovered after closing can't be undone.

faqs.q: What happens if funds accidentally route to me instead of the intermediary?
faqs.a: That can trigger constructive receipt, which risks disqualifying the entire exchange and making the sale taxable. We review closing statement language in advance specifically to prevent that from happening, and we flag any line item that would send funds anywhere other than the intermediary's escrow account.

faqs.q: Does the intermediary need to be based in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: No, qualified intermediaries commonly work with clients across state lines, and many Oklahoma City investors use an intermediary based elsewhere. What matters is that the escrow and agreement terms are set up correctly, not the intermediary's physical location, so we focus our review there.

faqs.q: How early should the exchange agreement be signed relative to closing?
faqs.a: It needs to be executed before your relinquished property closes, and we recommend having it finalized at least a few days ahead so there's no scramble at the closing table. Confirm exact timing with your intermediary based on their own process, since some require additional lead time for larger transactions.

faqs.q: What if I want to modify my identification list after submitting it?
faqs.a: You can revoke and resubmit an identification as long as you're still inside the 45-day window, but once that window closes, the list is fixed. We track your deadline closely so any changes happen with time to spare, rather than discovering a needed revision on day forty-four, and we send you a written reminder well ahead of the cutoff so the date never sneaks up on you.
